design_rationale: The SEND trial explicitly assigned eligible participants 1:1 using a central randomisation system and a computer minimisation program; the concurrent preference cohort was analyzed separately and is supportive rather than the main trial comparison.

domain_judgments.rationale: A central computer-based 1:1 minimisation procedure concealed allocation until telephone randomisation, and reported baseline characteristics were balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Allocation concealment was achieved using a central randomisation system. Patients were randomised (1:1 allocation) after research nurses telephoned Saving Faces, the trial co-ordinating centre. A minimisation computer program stratified patients by age (<40, 40–64, 65+years), tumour stage (T1 and T2) and surgeon.

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding was infeasible and 20 randomized patients did not receive or had unreported receipt of their assigned surgery, but the primary analyses appropriately used intention-to-treat and deviations were transparently reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In those randomised to have resection only, seven patients actually had a neck dissection as well and for another patient what they had was unreported. In those allocated to END, 12 had resection only... Primary analyses were by intention-to-treat (ITT).

domain_judgments.rationale: All 250 eligible randomized participants were included in the ITT efficacy analyses, follow-up was substantial, and attendance was similar between randomized groups, with no evident differential loss likely to bias survival outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Median follow-up was 57 months (25–75th centile 43–61 months). Similar numbers of patients in both trial groups attended each assessment visit.

domain_judgments.rationale: The principal outcomes, overall survival and disease-free survival, were clearly and objectively defined, measured using the same scheduled follow-up in both groups, and recurrence was generally supported by pathology or imaging, making assessor knowledge unlikely to materially bias results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was overall survival (OS; death from any cause...); Secondary outcomes included: disease-free survival (DFS: local, regional or distant recurrence, a new primary tumour or death from any cause, whichever occurred first...).

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered and primary, secondary, ITT, and prespecified per-protocol analyses were identified, but no accessible prespecified statistical analysis plan is provided here and several time horizons, adjusted/unadjusted models, subgroups, and post hoc analyses create some scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Primary analyses were by intention-to-treat (ITT). Prespecified per-protocol analyses were performed for patients who had the randomised surgical procedure.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns, driven by non-adherence/crossover in 20 randomized participants in an unblinded surgical trial and some potential flexibility in selecting among multiple analyses and time horizons. Central concealed randomization, balanced baseline groups, ITT analyses, near-complete survival follow-up, and objective outcomes otherwise support low risk.

design_rationale: This was explicitly described as a prospective randomized study, and patients were assigned within T1/T2 strata using sealed envelopes to observation or elective neck dissection.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although stratified sealed-envelope allocation and balanced measured baseline characteristics were reported, the method used to generate the sequence and safeguards ensuring opaque, sequentially numbered envelopes were not described, so allocation concealment cannot be confirmed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Two sets of sealed envelopes, 1 set for T1 patients and another set for T2 patients, were used for the randomization of patients to either observation or elective neck dissection.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and clinicians necessarily knew the surgical assignment, post-randomization adjuvant treatment varied according to pathological findings and acceptance, and one randomized participant was excluded rather than analyzed as assigned; however, these features do not clearly establish a material effect on the survival outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: One clinically T2 patient who was randomized to the observation arm was found to have pathologic T3 and therefore was excluded.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome ascertainment appears essentially complete for the 71 analyzed patients, with long follow-up, vital and recurrence status reported, and no loss to follow-up described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the other 53 patients who were still alive, none of them had tumor at the last follow-up; the minimum follow-up duration of these 53 patients was 34 months (mean, 86 months; longest, 122 months).

domain_judgments.rationale: Node-related mortality and disease-specific survival are appropriate outcomes and follow-up was structured, but outcome adjudication was not reported as blinded and surveillance differed between groups because observation patients received scheduled neck ultrasonography, creating some potential for differential detection of recurrence and cause-specific outcome classification.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of those patients on the observation arm, ultrasonographic examination of the neck was done every 3 months for the first 3 years.

domain_judgments.rationale: A trial registration and protocol were publicly posted only in 2005, after recruitment began in 1996 and near its completion in 2004, so prospective specification of outcomes and analyses cannot be verified despite the reported primary and secondary outcomes being clearly defined.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The research protocol was posted to the website of clinical trial public information center ofThe University ofHong Kong for public access of information in 2005.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. The main issues are incomplete reporting of sequence generation and allocation concealment, exclusion of one randomized patient, unavoidable lack of blinding with differential surveillance, and trial registration/protocol posting only after recruitment had ended; missing outcome data appear minimal.

design_rationale: The trial explicitly states that patients were randomly assigned 1:1 using a prepared computerized block design, with stratification by tumor site, stage, sex, and baseline ultrasonography findings.

domain_judgments.rationale: The computerized block sequence and stratification support random sequence generation and baseline groups were balanced, but the report does not describe allocation concealment or who generated and implemented the sequence.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were randomly assigned to undergo either elective or therapeutic neck dissection in a 1:1 ratio with the use of a prepared computerized block design.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although blinding was infeasible for these surgical strategies and a small number did not adhere, deviations were limited and the primary and secondary outcomes were analyzed according to intention to treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary and secondary end points were assessed in the intention-to-treat population

domain_judgments.rationale: Loss to follow-up was similar between groups but approximately 9–10% of participants were lost, and no analysis demonstrating that survival estimates were robust to informative missingness was reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The numbers of patients who were lost to follow-up were similar in the two groups (25 of 243 patients [10.3%] in elective-surgery group and 22 of 253 patients [8.7%] in the therapeutic-surgery group).

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome, death from any cause, is objective and was defined and measured identically from randomization in both groups, making bias from unblinded assessment unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary end point was overall survival, which was defined as the interval between the date of randomization and the date of death from any cause.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes and main analyses were prespecified and a protocol was available, but the reported analysis followed an unplanned interim analysis and a later DSMC-requested interim analysis of only the first 500 of 596 randomized patients, creating some potential for selective timing or analysis despite use of an alpha-spending function.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: An unplanned interim analysis (after the analysis of 248 patients and the occurrence of 43 deaths) was performed in 2011 after publication of a metaanalysis suggesting a benefit for elective neck dissection.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged to have some concerns, driven by absent reporting of allocation concealment, roughly 9–10% loss to follow-up without sensitivity analysis for informative censoring, and interim reporting after an unplanned earlier analysis. The objective primary outcome, balanced baseline characteristics, limited nonadherence, and intention-to-treat analysis otherwise reduce risk.

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that patients were stratified by T stage and randomized within each stage to resection alone or resection plus elective supraomohyoid neck dissection.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although random assignment stratified by T stage is explicitly reported, the sequence-generation method, allocation concealment, and group-specific baseline comparability are not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All 67 patients were stratified by stage, T1, N0; and T2, N0; and those in each stage were randomized to receive 1 of 2 types of treatment: resection alone (RA) or resection plus elective supraomohyoid neck dissection (RSOND).

domain_judgments.rationale: Post-randomization co-interventions differed substantially by group and were triggered by pathological or recurrent disease, while no intention-to-treat analysis or protocol-deviation information is reported; postoperative radiotherapy in the RSOND group could affect disease-free survival.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In our study, a low number of patients received radiotherapy: 7 patients (21%) of the RSOND group and 10 (30%) in the RA group. In the latter group, palliative radiotherapy was delivered to 8 of the 10 patients.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes are numerically reported for all 67 randomized patients, but completeness and duration of follow-up are not explicitly documented, and the text notes that some low-socioeconomic-status patients returned only with advanced recurrence.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This may be explained because this prospective study included a large number of low socioeconomic level patients who had returned to follow-up with advanced neck recurrence.

domain_judgments.rationale: Disease recurrence and survival are appropriate outcomes and appear to have been assessed similarly, but the surgical interventions could not be blinded and no blinded outcome adjudication or standardized surveillance schedule is reported, allowing possible differential detection of recurrence.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The impact of the two modalities of treatment on disease-free and overall survival was assessed by the Kaplan-Meier actuarial method and Wilcoxon's signed rank test.

domain_judgments.rationale: No protocol or prespecified analysis plan is reported, and numerous outcomes, subgroup factors, cut points, and statistical analyses were examined, including a tumor-thickness threshold based on the observed sample mean, creating substantial scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The mean thickness was 4 mm, and this dimension was used to divide the patients into two groups, those with tumor ≤4 mm (30 patients) and those with tumor >4 mm (37 patients).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because post-randomization co-interventions differed between groups without a clearly reported intention-to-treat approach, and there was substantial analytical flexibility and potential selective reporting without a prespecified protocol. Additional concerns arise from unreported allocation concealment, follow-up completeness, and blinded outcome assessment.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly allocated using previously generated random numbers to hemiglossectomy alone or hemiglossectomy plus ipsilateral radical neck dissection.

domain_judgments.rationale: A random-number sequence was used, but allocation concealment was not described, and the small analyzed groups showed some numerical baseline imbalances that are difficult to distinguish from chance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All T1-2 N0M0 patients... were randomized from previously generated random numbers to either hemiglossectomy alone (group A) or hemiglossectomy and ipsilateral radical neck dissection (group B).

domain_judgments.rationale: The analysis was not intention-to-treat: 14 of 73 randomized entrants did not complete initial treatment, and the reported comparison was further restricted to only 35 participants who completed treatment and at least one year of follow-up; treatment-related co-interventions also varied according to post-randomization findings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 73 patients have been entered into the protocol to date. Twelve patients did not take treatment after entry and two patients were declared unfit for surgery. Thus, 59 patients have completed initial treatment. Thirty-five of these patients who have completed a minimum of 1 year of follow-up after completion of treatment have been analysed.

domain_judgments.rationale: Disease-free survival was reported for only 35 of 73 trial entrants, with 24 treated participants excluded because they had not yet reached one year of follow-up and no group-specific accounting or analysis showing that missing outcomes could not bias the result.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Thus, 59 patients have completed initial treatment. Thirty-five of these patients who have completed a minimum of 1 year of follow-up after completion of treatment have been analysed.

domain_judgments.rationale: Disease-free survival is an appropriate outcome and all patients were personally followed, but outcome assessment was apparently unblinded and no standardized or blinded adjudication process was reported, allowing possible differential detection of recurrence between surgical strategies.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All patients were personally followed by one of the authors (A.R.F.).

domain_judgments.rationale: No protocol, registration, prespecified outcome definition, time point, or analysis plan was reported, and several disease-free survival subgroup comparisons were presented, leaving scope for selective choice of analyses in this interim report.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This paper presents the first report of an ongoing prospective randomised clinical trial... Though the study is an ongoing one and the median follow-up period is only 22 months, some observations can be made based on our findings.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by exclusion of 14 randomized entrants from treatment and restriction of the outcome analysis to 35 of 73 entrants who had completed treatment and at least one year of follow-up, without intention-to-treat analysis or evidence that unavailable outcomes were unbiased. Unreported allocation concealment, unblinded outcome assessment, and lack of a prespecified analysis plan add further concerns.
